text:
Alex Morgan: Quick brain-dump: proposing a hybrid reserve+spot routing policy that biases short-lived steady traffic to cheaper spot pools but preserves SLOs during churn via a 'reserve-holdback' and fast variant fallback. Wanted early feedback before I write a rollout PR.

Priya Kapoor: high level sounds good. can you sketch when we'd cross to reserved vs cross-region? how does customer tier affect the decision?

Alex Morgan: good q. idea is: local spot preferred for normal requests. if eviction probability > threshold OR observed latency degradation > X, we 1) try soft failover to local reserved lanes (warm reserve) for N seconds, 2) if reserved unavailable, route to model-variant (quantized / lower context) in same region, 3) finally cross-region to fallback region reserved capacity. Tiers: platinum -> skip variant fallback (prefer reserved), standard -> allow variant, free -> variant + best-effort reserved.

Ben Liu: love the tier mapping. suggest adding a short "grace window" after a predicted eviction where we keep prefix cache and only spill new requests to reserve to avoid KV cache thrash. basically: hold for 3s, then spill.

Sara Jones: can we get concrete numbers? last week APAC spot evictions had a 12% spike for 7 minutes and p95 gen latency moved from 140ms -> 380ms. infra-bot posted metric dump.

infra-bot: ALERT: 1976-05-12 03:14 UTC - APAC spot eviction rate 12.1% over 7m, regional reserved utilization 78%, cross-region egress steady. recent preemptible churn shows correlation with specific instance families.

Alex Morgan: thanks @Sara — so config needs to check three signals: eviction_rate, reserved_headroom, and p95_latency drift. If eviction_rate > 8% && reserved_headroom > 15% -> fail to reserved. If reserved_headroom < 15% -> try model-variant. If both exhausted -> cross-region.

Priya Kapoor: model-variant fallback concerns: output quality regression for some customers. How do we force variant only for non-SLA routes?

Ben Liu: route config should be per-route override. e.g., API routes can carry `route_preferences` with allowed fallbacks. Default: allow quantized-variant for embeddings/rerank, disallow for completions with safety-critical outputs.

Alex Morgan: here's a rough example of the routing policy I'm thinking (pseudo-yaml):

```yaml
policy_name: hybrid-reserve-holdback
signals:
  - eviction_rate: 0.08
  - reserved_headroom_pct: 0.15
  - latency_drift_ms: 200
behavior:
  - if: eviction_rate > signals.eviction_rate and reserved_headroom_pct > signals.reserved_headroom_pct
    then: route -> reserved_local (warm)
    holdback_seconds: 3
  - else if: reserved_headroom_pct <= signals.reserved_headroom_pct
    then: route -> model_variant_quantized
  - else: route -> cross_region_reserved
route_overrides:
  customer_tiers:
    platinum: prefer_reserved_skip_variant: true
    standard: allow_variant: true
    free: allow_variant: true
```

Ben Liu: nit: add a TTL on "holdback" so hot prefixes don't stay pinned forever. also track token-cost delta when switching to quantized variant.

Sara Jones: operationally, we need runbook steps for a spike: detect -> notify -> 1-click force to reserved -> rollback. Can the console show per-route fallback counts?

Alex Morgan: yes, console should expose metrics: fallback_count, avg_fallback_latency, avg_token_cost_change, customer_impact_score. I'll add those to the dashboard ticket.

Priya Kapoor: rollout plan? small canary in us-west1 for low-traffic models, then progressive ramp with abort on error budget burn. also need a test harness to replay eviction traces so we can validate correctness.

Alex Morgan: proposed rollout:
- canary 2% traffic (non-platinum) in us-west1 for 48h
- evaluate fallback counts, p95 latency, cost-per-token delta
- ramp 10% every 24h if no regression
- block ramp if error budget > 20% or user-impact-score > threshold

infra-bot: NOTE: replay tool available in /tools/eviction-simulator (use --trace apac-2026-05-05).

Ben Liu: one more thing — batching interplay. mixing pooling strategies can change batch composition. we should instrument per-batch pool_id so we can see if spot->reserve transitions cause smaller batches (costly).

Sara Jones: APAC followup: need faster cross-region path for short-timeouts (low-latency apps). consider keeping a small hot-warm leased slice in eu-west for APAC critical customers as a last-resort low-latency cross-region option. 

Alex Morgan: agreed. call it "fast-bridge" reserved slice. allocate per-customer policy when they opt in. pricing & agreements TBD.

Priya Kapoor: sounds actionable. I can take the tiers/fallback policy and write the per-route schema. Alex can you open the infra PR with default thresholds and the holdback wiring?

Alex Morgan: will do. PR target: infra/routing repo. plan to include metrics, dashboard links, and runbook draft. writing it up this afternoon. thanks for the quick feedback everyone. :thumbsup:

Ben Liu: :thumbsup: ping me for canary validation.

Sara Jones: adding runbook item to oncall checklist. good work.

infra-bot: THREAD_SUMMARY: hybrid-reserve-holdback proposal, canary plan, runbook + dashboard items created; infra PR expected.
